title: Repeated-measures ANOVA
biology: Physiologists measure the same animals at four assay temperatures.
design: Each of 24 animals provides all four measurements.
question: Are mean oxygen-use rates equal across temperatures within animals?
null: All four population temperature means are equal.
options: Treat condition as a factor for a general timepoint comparison
The endpoint contrast is prespecified separately
assumptions: Sphericity for the usual repeated-measures F test
Appropriate residual behavior and complete measurements
parametric: Use a sphericity correction when needed
An LMM supports a more flexible covariance structure
nonparametric: Friedman compares within-subject ranks in complete blocks
A within-block permutation must preserve the assignment design

plot_args.note: Connect measurements from the same animal

practice: Why does ignoring subject ID create the wrong analysis?
code_simulate:
set.seed(2103)
d <- expand.grid(temperature = c(15, 20, 25, 30), subject = 1:24)
individual <- rnorm(24, 0, 2)
d$oxygen <- 8 + .35 * (d$temperature - 15) +
  individual[d$subject] + rnorm(nrow(d), 0, 1.3)
write.csv(d, file.path(output_dir, "data.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
code_plot:
p <- ggplot(d, aes(temperature, oxygen)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = subject), color = "#A9B5B8", alpha = .55) +
  geom_point(color = "#246A73", alpha = .6, size = 1.8) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "line", color = "#B7663E", linewidth = 1.7) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", color = "#B7663E", size = 3.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(15, 20, 25, 30)) +
  labs(x = "Assay temperature (°C)", y = "Oxygen use (µmol/hour)",
       caption = "Gray lines preserve individuals; orange line shows means") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 16)
print(p)
code_analysis:
fit <- aov(oxygen ~ condition + Error(subject/condition), data = d)
summary(fit)
endpoints <- t.test(d$oxygen[d$temperature == 30],
                   d$oxygen[d$temperature == 15], paired = TRUE)
generating_model: 24 animals are measured at 15, 20, 25 and 30°C. Oxygen use = 8 + 0.35 × (temperature − 15) + an animal-specific Normal(0, 2²) intercept + independent Normal(0, 1.3²) observation error. Intercepts are shared within animals, producing repeated-measure dependence and a spherical covariance structure. No rounding is applied.
generating_truth: Population means are 8, 9.75, 11.5 and 13.25 µmol/hour. The endpoint difference is 5.25 µmol/hour and the equal-means null is false.

columns.name: subject
columns.meaning: Animal measured at all four temperatures

teaching_point: The subject ID, not the row, defines independent replication.
